learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge of fluid mechanics.
Increase knowledge in the field of industrial engineering with particular focus on thermofluid-dynamics.

Develop awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering with particular focus on the issues related to the conversion, transmission, final use of energy and to the design of fluid machines and energy systems.
Be able to face engineering problems by means of suitable and well-timed methodologies and techniques related to fluid mechanics in the industrial sector.
Acquire basic knowledge of the fluid dynamics governing equation.
Ability to evaluate for simple systems the fluid dynamics loads.
Ability to perform fluid dynamics analyses on simple steady state systems using the control volume technique.
Develop the ability of solving physical and engineering problems adopting a scientific approach.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: The field of fluid mechanics
Solution of problems regarding the evaluation of hydrostatic forces and moments on flat and curved surfaces
Exercises on the control volume method and about the Bernoulli’s Theorem
Analytical solution of the Navier-Stokes equations for some simple problems
Viscous flows in ducts, laminar and turbulent flow regimes, distributed and minor losses
assessment_rules: The assessment is performed via a written and oral examination. Admission to the oral examination is subordinate to passing the written examination. The grading scheme is based on a scale of 30 points, with successful completion ranging from 18 to 30. The final grade is determined by the oral examination, which is the sum of grades obtained from answering two questions. For students with disabilities/invalidity or specific learning disorder (DSA), exam methods will be adapted.
